title: QBR - ACME Analytics Health Check
next_steps: Maya to send updated cost & usage report for last 3 months by 2025-02-21
Omar to run latency benchmark against ACME ingest pipeline and share raw results by 2025-02-25
Linda to schedule roadmap sync with ACME product and PMs for week of 2025-03-03
action_items: Maya Chen: prepare breakdown of token volumes by route + recommended batching knobs by 2025-02-21
Omar Patel: investigate KV cache hit-rate drop and propose config changes by 2025-02-24
Priya Singh (ACME): share recent traffic spike logs and affected endpoints by 2025-02-20
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage, cost trends, recent incidents, and roadmap alignment. ACME is generally happy with latency but flagged cost overruns on high-volume routes and a recent cache miss incident. Redwood to provide cost optimization suggestions and run targeted benchmarks.
topics: roadmap alignment and upcoming features (rollouts, observability)
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining our QBR, appreciate you all making time. We'll try to keep this to about 45 minutes and then leave time for QA.
[00:18] Carlos Rivera: Yep thanks Maya, appreciate it. We have Priya and Tom on the line as well, and Jenna from product.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Great, quick agenda: usage & cost trends, reliability notes, roadmap asks, then open items. Linda will capture next steps.
[01:15] Linda Park: Hi all, recording and notes on, I'll drop links after call. Also we'll share the cost spreadsheet referenced in the invite.
[02:02] Omar Patel: Quick intro from me, I'm the SE who worked on your initial onboarding and the perf tuning on the embedding routes.
[02:45] Priya Singh: Cool, to start, we've seen token spend double month over month on the recommendations route, not sure why the volume jump happened.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Okay let's pull the usage chart — I have the dashboard here. Looks like two things: a higher QPS and longer average seq lengths for a subset of requests.
[03:42] Carlos Rivera: Right there's been a new feature that sends 3x longer context for cold-start recs, that was rolled without batching changes.
[04:05] Omar Patel: That makes sense — longer sequences dramatically change throughput and cost. We recommended changing batching and enabling prefix caching but I don't see the config applied.
[04:38] Tom Hsu: We didn't apply those yet because we were worried about latency tradeoffs during peak.
[05:00] Maya Chen: Understood. We can simulate different batch settings; Omar can run a quick benchmark to show latency vs tokens cost so you can pick a sweet spot.
[05:30] Priya Singh: That'd be helpful. Also we hit a reliability incident last week — a cache miss storm that spiked p99 to 1.2s.
[06:02] Omar Patel: Yes I pulled the incident traces. There was an unexpected eviction pattern when your traffic pattern changed, caused by small KV cache capacity on the pool.
[06:35] Maya Chen: Can you summarize remediation and longer term fix please?

[06:50] Omar Patel: Short term we increased cache capacity on the dedicated pool which brought p99 down. Long term options: bump KV cache size, enable adaptive prefetching, or use a larger instance sku. There's also a config to pin hot prefixes to avoid eviction churn.
[07:25] Carlos Rivera: What are the cost implications of bumping cache vs larger instance? We want minimal opex increase.

[07:40] Maya Chen: Good question — increasing KV cache size on the same pool is cheaper than adding another GPU node. I'll send a cost delta table. Also Redwood Optimize has recommendations for this workload.
[08:05] Jenna Morales: From product side we need predictable SLAs; that p99 spike caused customer complaints. If the fix costs more, we need to understand ROI.
[08:30] Linda Park: Note: action item - Maya to send cost delta + recommended config, due 2/21.
[09:00] Priya Singh: Another thing — we're evaluating Dedicated vs staying on Hosted. Our security folks want VPC peering for Private, but timeline is 6-9 months.
[09:28] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can provide reserved capacity and lower unit cost for sustained throughput; Private/VPC is possible for on-prem/policy, but will require a scoping engagement.
[09:55] Carlos Rivera: Is there a hard threshold when Dedicated becomes cheaper? We can look at a 12-month commit.

[10:12] Omar Patel: Rough rule: if steady state token and inference throughput exceed X tokens/day and sustained GPU utilization is high, Dedicated often reduces per-token cost vs Hosted. I'll generate a model for your numbers.
[10:45] Priya Singh: Please include burst scenarios because our traffic is spiky — we can't lose headroom.
[11:10] Maya Chen: We'll model both committed baseline + burst credits. Also, redistributing some routes to smaller quantized variants can save cost for less-critical outputs.
[11:45] Tom Hsu: We had questions about audit logs and KMS integration for Private — security needs to see certs and SOC 2 evidence.
[12:05] Maya Chen: Linda will send our security pack and SOC 2 report. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via our dedicated/private deployment options.
[12:30] Jenna Morales: Good. On roadmap, we're interested in rollout controls and canary policies to push smaller model variants gradually.
[12:55] Omar Patel: Rollouts are supported — can do percentage-based canaries and automatic fallback. We can demo that in a follow-up session.
[13:20] Priya Singh: That would be great. Also we're tracking a quality regression alert we saw when updating a prompt template.
[13:40] Maya Chen: We can tie evals to your prompt sets and surface regression alerts in Redwood Console. Linda, add a demo for evals to the follow-up.
[14:05] Linda Park: Noted, I'll schedule. Action: demo evals + rollouts, target week of 3/3.
[14:30] Carlos Rivera: Back to costs — we saw unexpected charges labeled 'embedding-index' — what's driving those tokens?
[14:55] Omar Patel: Likely periodic re-embedding pipelines or retries. We saw higher retries on failed batches which doubled token spend. Could be transient errors upstream.
[15:20] Priya Singh: We'll correlate with our ETL logs and share by 2/20.
[15:42] Maya Chen: Great. So immediate items: cost report, benchmark for batching, investigate cache miss root cause, share security docs, schedule rollouts/evals demo.
[16:05] Tom Hsu: One last technical ask — can we get a raw trace export for the incident to ingest into our observability stack?
[16:25] Omar Patel: Yes we can export traces. I'll prepare a sanitized export and include spans mapping.
[16:50] Maya Chen: Awesome. Any blockers on deliverables?
[17:05] Carlos Rivera: No blockers, timeline is mostly internal approvals for Dedicated. We'll review the cost model once you send it.
[17:25] Priya Singh: Also want a short runbook for troubleshooting cache issues so our SREs can respond faster.
[17:40] Omar Patel: We'll provide a runbook and quick playbook for the KV cache scenarios.
[18:00] Linda Park: I'll capture all these as action items and share notes + links to the dashboard after the call.

[18:15] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Quick recap: Maya to send cost delta & usage breakdown; Omar to run benchmarks and prepare trace export + runbook; Linda to schedule rollouts/evals demo and send security pack. We'll reconvene after you review the cost model.
[18:45] Carlos Rivera: Sounds good, thanks all.
[19:00] Jenna Morales: Thanks, bye.
[19:05] [Meeting ended]
